identity.title: Harden verified-feature commit and version governance

origin.summary: The owner requested stricter version control so only completed, verified, and documented features are committed and pushed.

state.current_summary: Verified-feature governance is documented and enforced by the expanded CI gate; the qualified feature, governance, and headless-check commits are pushed to main and the exact remote head passed the complete Windows workflow.

objective.summary: Make verified feature commits, product-version movement, release qualification, publication, and public readback distinct and auditable states.
constraints: Do not change the product version, create a tag, or publish a release without a separately approved release candidate.
Reuse the existing centralized MSBuild version source and existing verification commands instead of adding a duplicate version system.
Keep public documentation OpenVisionLab-owned and exclude private research, vendor comparisons, and local test artifacts.
Commit only the currently verified PL-0019 through PL-0022 scope and its governance documentation.

criteria.text: Repository rules define when a feature may be committed, when separate feature commits are required, and the bounded exception for inseparable jointly verified changes.
Version policy and changelog distinguish development identity, verified commit, release candidate qualification, publication, and public readback without moving the current product version.
Windows CI runs the newest stage-timing, Source Quality, Completeness cell-export, ordered Run, history, unrelated-export, and structure regression gates.
Documentation, YAML, Proofline, diff, Release build, focused checks, commit scope, and remote push are verified and recorded.

context.summary: Product and assembly version already have one central source and should not be duplicated.
The existing policy owns semantic versioning, release candidates, contract versions, tags, and release gates.
The current workflow has broad legacy coverage but does not invoke the newest Run Record contract verifiers.

evidence.observation: Repository rules now require resolved scope, current focused verification, proportional build, owning documentation, valid JSON/links, diff hygiene, explicit staging, and one independently releasable feature per commit, with a bounded jointly verified common-contract exception.

The policy and new CHANGELOG.md keep product version 0.1.1-dev while separating verified commit, pushed baseline, CI qualification, frozen candidate, publication, and public readback; the existing single MSBuild version source is retained without a redundant bump script.

The new CI command set ran locally after a Debug solution build with 0 warnings and 0 errors: Completeness 30/30, artifact-owned Runner 19/19, Surface Match 23/23, Source Quality 18/18, ordered Run 15/15, history 12/12, and structure 29/29 all passed.

Commits e6e3776 (qualified PL-0019 through PL-0022 feature scope), 7da72bd (version governance), and 81e835f (deterministic headless Workbench verification) were pushed to main. Local final qualification passed a Release solution build with 0 warnings and 0 errors, all six current Workbench checks (87/87, 64/64, 84/84, 52/52, 6/6, 40/40), Proofline validation, and git diff hygiene. Remote main exactly matched 81e835fc98850e9ca3c82f12b367c648912599b5, and Windows CI run 32093834200 completed successfully including both current Workbench and new Run Record contract steps.

events.summary: Resolved after the documented commit/version gates, expanded Run Record CI coverage, three intentional main commits, and the exact pushed head all passed local and hosted verification.
